blogs.title: When the Chest Hides the Belly: Pancreatopleural Fistula and the Pulmonary Mask
blogs.description: A deep dive into how pancreatic pathology can present with purely thoracic symptoms, the anatomical pathways that create this 'mask' (tracking through the aortic and esophageal hiatuses), and why PPF is consistently misdiagnosed on initial presentation. Includes practical guidance on when to broaden your differential beyond thoracic causes in recurrent pleural effusion.

blogs.title: Pleural Fluid Amylase: The Single Test That Changed Everything
blogs.description: An exploration of pleural fluid amylase as an underutilized diagnostic tool in effusion workup. Covers what constitutes a diagnostic level (≥1000 IU/L being pathognomonic for PPF), the differential diagnosis of amylase-rich effusions including malignancy and esophageal perforation, and why pancreatic-type vs. salivary-type amylase matters.

blogs.title: Bicycle Handlebar Trauma: A Classic Mechanism for Pediatric Pancreatic Injury
blogs.description: A focused review of bicycle handlebar injuries as an important mechanism of blunt abdominal trauma in children, why pancreatic injury is often initially occult, and the delayed presentations clinicians should anticipate. Discusses the anatomy that makes the pancreas vulnerable and the importance of trauma history even weeks after the event.

blogs.title: Third Time's the Charm: When to Re-take the History
blogs.description: A reflection on the importance of persistent history-taking in recurrent presentations. This child's trauma history only emerged on the third admission after repeated interviews. Discusses strategies for eliciting key information when initial workup is negative, the psychology of why patients withhold information, and how to avoid premature closure.

blogs.title: PPF Management: From NPO to Surgery - A Practical Algorithm
blogs.description: A practical guide to managing pancreatopleural fistula based on available evidence in the absence of standardized pediatric guidelines. Covers the stepwise approach from conservative measures (bowel rest, TPN, octreotide) with only 12% success in children, to ERCP with stenting (approaching 100% success), to surgical options like distal pancreatectomy. Discusses timing and indications for escalation.
